text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia on Tuesday fixed the crown stronger against the market showing its commitment to support the currency if neccessary, dealers said.

- Interior Minister Gustav Krajci has asked President Michal Kovac to postpone a referendum on direct presidential elections until the Constitutional Court rules on the request by deputies for a ruling on whether the constitution can be changed by a referendum.
- President Kovac rejected Krajci's request saying the referendum must be carried out regardless of what will be the Constitutional Court ruling.

- Rudolf Schuster, mayor of the second largest Slovak city of Kosice, eastern Slovakia, said he would submit his candidacy in next year's presidential elections if the planned referendum introduces a direct citizens vote of the president.
- The Czech engineering company CKD Praha said it would present its project for building an underground transport system in the Slovak capital Bratislava.
- The Slovak government on Tuesday approved a draft law which should enable the state to impose unspecified measures to limit imports of goods that are also produced in Slovakia.

PRAVDA - The paper quotes ruling coalition sources as saying some deputies of two minor coalition parties, the ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS) and the ultra-right Slovak National party (SNS), wanted the dismissal of National Property Fund President Stefan Gavornik and the Minister of Justice Jozef Liscak.

- Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic said the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) wanted citizens to vote in favour of NATO membership in a referendum on the question scheduled for next weekend.

- The Constitutional Court is expected to rule on Wednesday on the request by deputies of the ruling coalition whether the consitution can be changed by a referendum. Deputies submitted the request in an attempt to cancel the referendum on direct presidential elections.

- President Michal Kovac said a negative answer in a referendum on NATO membership would be a "catastrophe" for Slovakia, since the result of the plebiscite would be valid for the next three years without any chance for the government or the parliament to change it.
SME - Major Slovak opposition parties have repeatedly called for citizens to vote "yes" both for integration in NATO and for direct presidential elections.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Output of the Slovak engineering sector should total some 99 billion crowns a year in 2000 rising further to 161.6 billion crowns in the year 2005.
